Quick mapping from the matrix — high level gaps per marketplace: 

AWS:
- Billing & Tax: bank account + W9 (US) or W-8 if non-US — Zenith provided banking details but no W9.
- Security: AWS requires SOC2 Type II or bridge letter; executive summary alone likely insufficient.
- Marketplace listing: product SKU and AMI/container image location needed (they noted a container registry but not a public artifact).

GCP:
- Billing: tax docs similar to AWS; GCP also needs VAT handling for EU customers if applicable.
- Security: GCP listing allows summary but we will require SOC2 report for enterprise customers.
- Support SLAs: need a documented support email + escalation path.

Azure:
- Legal: Azure Marketplace expects commercial terms + Microsoft reseller paperwork if they plan to use co-sell.
- Technical: Azure requires VM images/ARM templates or offer container images and test that images install.

Action items I can own: compile a 1-page gap matrix and mark which items we can accept vs need additional docs. Will have that by EOD tomorrow.

Vanessa
Senior Marketplace Ops
Redwood Inference

P.S. tagging Camila for PO flow confirmation and Kimberly for legal acceptance criteria.

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Thanks folks — quick procurement & activation notes from my side: 

1) PO process:
 - For a standard marketplace listing that will be billed to customers via Redwood-hosted flows, we do NOT require a separate PO for listing itself.
 - For Dedicated/Reserved capacity purchases (customer committing to a contract for capacity) we typically require a PO + signed commercial terms. If Zenith plans to sell Reserved capacity via marketplace, they should prepare to accept PO invoicing.

2) FinOps/tax:
 - We need W9 (or W-8BEN) and a remit-to address before final activation. If they have a VAT ID for EU sales, include that in the spreadsheet.

3) Timeline & mutual action plan (suggested):
 - Day 0: Zenith confirms missing docs (W9, SOC2 redaction/bridge letter, image location).
 - Day 3: Redwood provides gap matrix and exact artifact specs (we will link to example artifacts).
 - Day 7: Vendor supplies missing deliverables.
 - Day 10-14: Validation + marketplace listing prep.

Kimberly — can Legal confirm whether a SOC2 summary + signed attestation from their auditor is acceptable as a short-term measure for sales demo customers?

Camila Reyes
Marketplace Enablement Lead | Redwood Inference

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cOnboardingMatrix (draft matrix)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial intake — onboarding forms for Redwood marketplace listing

Short yes/no on legal evidence: 
- SOC2: executive summary alone is NOT sufficient for enterprise-level customers. We can accept a redacted SOC2 Type II if the redactions are limited to customer-specific data or IP; otherwise we need either a full SOC2 under NDA or a bridge letter from the auditor confirming coverage.
- Attestation letter: acceptable as an interim step for demos and small pilots, provided it includes auditor contact info and scope dates.
- Commercial terms: for Reserved/Dedicated we will require a signed order form or PO + signature; marketplace listing alone does not create a billing relationship for Reserved capacity.

Next steps: I will draft a short checklist (1 page) outlining acceptable evidence and an example attestation that vendors can sign. Will post to the shared drive and cc the vendor when complete.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
